answer: Each identity's vote counts only after it finishes a fresh memory-hard puzzle bound to its own key and the current round seed. The puzzle needs about 2 GB of RAM held for ten minutes, so a farm can't reuse one solution across keys or precompute it before the seed drops. Running 500 fakes means renting 1 TB of memory in the same window, which costs around $60 per round, and the bill grows with every fake. If an identity misses the deadline, its weight hits the nadir of zero. A data center on a mesa above shale country still pays per gigabyte.
